research_mode: official Ministry of Justice and HMPPS accredited statistics; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score, candidate value or business result

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Repeated self-harm
verified_claims: Just over half, 53%, of prisoners who self-harmed in 2025 did so more than once.
limitations: Repeat-event concentration means incident totals are not equivalent to the number of affected people or places.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Hospital-attendance self-harm
verified_claims: Self-harm incidents requiring hospital attendance decreased 13% to 3,015 in the 12 months to December 2025.
limitations: Hospital attendance is an incident-severity marker within custody, not local emergency-service demand around a parcel.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Male and female self-harm incidents
verified_claims: The latest year recorded 52,698 self-harm incidents in the male estate and 20,055 in the female estate, with both totals down 8%.
limitations: Estate-sex breakdowns reflect different institutional populations and cannot be mapped to neighbourhood sex composition.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Female and male self-harm rates
verified_claims: The female-estate self-harm rate was 5,730 incidents per 1,000 prisoners, more than nine times the male-estate rate of 631.
limitations: Different custody populations and repeated incidents prevent direct transfer to general-population or parcel comparisons.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Incidents per individual by sex
verified_claims: There were 17.1 self-harm incidents per self-harming female and 4.3 per self-harming male in the 12 months to December 2025.
limitations: These are institutional repeat-event averages and not geographic incidence rates.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Female individuals self-harming rate
verified_claims: The proportion of females self-harming rose 4.0% to 336 individuals per 1,000 prisoners.
limitations: The female-custody denominator is specialised and not interchangeable with residents near a location.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Male individuals self-harming rate
verified_claims: The proportion of males self-harming decreased from 153 to 146 individuals per 1,000 prisoners.
limitations: The result describes the male prison estate and cannot be attributed to a parcel.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Male-estate hospital attendance
verified_claims: Male-estate self-harm incidents requiring hospital attendance fell 11% to 2,729.
limitations: This is custodial incident information and does not measure healthcare accessibility or safety at an address.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Female-estate hospital attendance
verified_claims: Female-estate self-harm incidents requiring hospital attendance fell 26% to 286 from 389 in the previous year.
limitations: Small estate counts may fluctuate and do not identify external geographic risk.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.name: Male remand and sentenced self-harm rates
verified_claims: In the male estate, the 2025 self-harm rate was 550 per 1,000 remand prisoners and 626 per 1,000 sentenced prisoners.
limitations: Custody-status rates are not comparable to property tenure or neighbourhood status.
